Subject: Medicore SSQ — PII segmentation & egress controls

Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our SSQ. A few quick clarifying questions before we complete our compliance review:

1) Tenant/PII segmentation: can you confirm how customer PII is logically/physically separated from telemetry and model telemetry? We need specifics on isolation boundaries (process, storage, network) for our DPA.

2) Transient caches / KV: what is the default TTL for in-memory KV caches used for prefix caching and streaming sessions? Any behavior where caches persist beyond session end?

3) Egress & subprocessors: your subprocessor roster lists several CDNs/edge partners — do any of those vendors perform tokenized data caching or store prompt history? If so, which vendors and locations?

4) Cross-border routing: if a customer opts for multi-region routing, how do you ensure no PII egress to regions disallowed under our policy?

5) Key custody: brief note on whether Redwood or customer holds CMKs for hosted deployments.

Can you send a short dataflow diagram (ingest -> processing -> storage -> telemetry) and point to any annex language we can include in the Medicore DPA? Ideally by end of week.

Attachments: Medicore_SSQ_v3.pdf (our completed questionnaire)

Cheers,
Alice Turner
Data Protection Officer
Medicore

Subject: Re: Medicore SSQ — PII segmentation & egress controls

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Putting answers inline and attaching a short packet (SSQ answers + v3 dataflow). Forwarding to Marissa and Neha for any procurement/ops notes.

1) Tenant/PII segmentation:
- Logical separation: customer data flows into isolated ingestion queues tagged with tenant_id. Processing occurs in containerized runtimes with per-tenant namespace isolation (K8s namespaces + RBAC).
- Storage: model I/O (prompts/responses) for hosted customers is written to per-tenant object buckets where enabled; default behavior is ephemeral storage only. Telemetry (metrics/aggregates) is written to a separate telemetry cluster that strips tenant identifiers by default.
- Network: internal VPC routing and security groups prevent direct access between tenant buckets and telemetry clusters.

2) Transient caches / KV:
- Default in-memory KV cache TTL is 300 seconds (5 minutes) for streaming/prefix caches.
- For sessions where streaming exceeds 250 tokens, the runtime swaps older KV frames to encrypted local ephemeral storage which is deleted at session termination; no long-term persistence unless customer explicitly enables conversation history.

3) Egress & subprocessors:
- Current subprocessors that may touch prompt text (transiently) are: EdgeCache Inc (edge caching for low-latency read-only prompt fragments) and LogStream Partners (aggregated telemetry). Both operate under data processing agreements; EdgeCache does not persist full conversation history — only short prompt fragments used for cache keys; fragments are TTLed <1 hour and are pseudonymized.
- Locations: EdgeCache has EU and US POPs — we can restrict use to region-specific POPs per-customer routing policy.

4) Cross-border routing:
- Routing policy is configurable at the account level. If Medicore requires region-exclusion, we can pin traffic to specific regions and enforce no-fallback to other regions; we also provide routing proofs (trace logs) as evidence for audits.

5) Key custody:
- Hosted default: Redwood-managed CMKs in an HSM with strict access controls; customer side: we support BYOK (customer-managed keys) via KMS integration for customers who require sole custody.

Next steps:
- Attached: medicore_ssq_answers_20280605.pdf (our completed SSQ answers) and dataflow_diagram_v3.png (annotated).
- If helpful, we can add a short annex clause for the Medicore DPA that restricts EdgeCache POP selection and documents TTLs. Suggest a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the DPA team through the diagram.

Attachments: medicore_ssq_answers_20280605.pdf (PDF), dataflow_diagram_v3.png (PNG)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

If you can add the answers inline in the PDF or send a short note, we can close the routing/egress questions and move to DPA annex language.

Alice — quick tech annex below (I also updated the PDF with these lines and re-attached an annex text file).

KV eviction / deletion model:
- Deletion model: ephemeral swap files are deleted synchronously at session termination. The runtime issues a delete call to the ephemeral store and verifies response; for durability reasons (in rare storage-layer edge cases) we additionally run a background GC sweep within 60 minutes to remove any residual artifacts. We record a deletion event in the audit log with timestamp and object id.

EdgeCache replication:
- EdgeCache POPs: fragments are strictly stored within POPs and are not replicated to other POPs or our control plane in plaintext. EdgeCache sends aggregated cache-miss telemetry (counts, latencies) to LogStream Partners; this telemetry is numeric-only and contains no raw prompt text or tenant IDs.
- We have a contractual clause requiring EdgeCache to limit replication and to TTL all fragments; we can include the vendor clause in the annex.

Audit evidence & routing proofs:
- We can provide a short export of routing traces for a 30-day window showing POP selection per-request (redacted to hide client IPs) as part of the DPA evidence pack.

Attachments included in this message: ssq_annex_kms_note.txt (text annex with BYOK language), dataflow_diagram_v3.png (annotated), medicore_ssq_answers_20280605.pdf (updated).
